what_happened: The job "Add incremental attribution checking with checkpoints and full replay" (20261024-220048-engm) failed in planning, before any code was written. After round 3 of 3 the critic still said the plan needed revising. The critic's headline verdict says the reading misread the request, because it moved the timings the request wanted on this repository to a synthetic fixture of about 200 landings and deferred the real-repository timing. The same text then says the user accepted this, so it is a known deviation and not a misreading. The critic judged the rest of the plan sound and grounded in code. Checkpoint exists in history.rs, check_attribution and walk still do the full read and full audit_history, each demonstration would fail without its behavior, and CI stays read-only. Four findings remained, all minor or nit. The range audit of the records branch is undecided, and audit_history takes no range. The step order in the fixture timing test is ambiguous. The timings come from a synthetic fixture, not from this repository. Read-only mode forced by the CI variable is silent. The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria, no blocker or major findings and no failed checks. Nothing was delivered.
cause: The planning loop passes or fails on the critic's overall verdict, not on the severity of its findings. Nothing says that a plan with only minor findings and nits passes. Nothing records a user-accepted deviation, such as the synthetic timing fixture, where the critic can see it, so the critic treats it as a misreading. It is raised again each round. The critic's verdict can also contradict its own findings, calling something a misreading and then a known deviation. The three-round cap has no fallback: open questions the planner could settle (such as how to do the range audit) are left open, no partial plan is kept, and a retry starts without the critic's earlier findings. This is a wider planning-stage weakness than any one plan gap. The earlier failed planning jobs on this branch ended at the same cap.
prevention: Make the planning gate decide from structured findings in code. A plan passes when it has no blocker or major finding, and minor findings and nits are carried into the producer brief as notes. Add a field for user-accepted deviations to the reading. The critic is shown it, and a finding that restates an accepted deviation is dropped by the gate. Reject a critic verdict that contradicts its own findings. Require the planner to settle open questions before the last round. Keep the last plan so a retry can start from it.
proposed_request: Change the planning stage gate so a plan passes when the critic reports no blocker or major findings. Carry minor findings and nits into the producer's brief as notes, and do not fail the job on them. Record deviations from the request that the user has accepted in the accepted reading, show them to the critic, and have the gate drop any critic finding that restates one. Treat a critic verdict that says "needs revising" with only minor findings or nits as a pass with notes. Keep the last plan and the critic's findings when planning ends without a pass, and give them to a retry. Demonstrate it with tests. A plan with only minor findings passes. A plan with a major finding still fails. A finding that restates an accepted deviation is dropped. A retry receives the earlier findings. Then retry the job "Add incremental attribution checking with checkpoints and full replay" (20261024-220048-engm), with the synthetic-fixture timing recorded as an accepted deviation.
